     6	/-!
     7	# Z-point deficits of the evaluated pair-line measurement
     8	
     9	This module bounds the deficit of the overlap between the evaluated paired-line
    10	measurement and the expanded Z-point measurement. The proof inserts the completed
    11	joint point measurement, replaces it by the X-then-Z ordered product, and sums
    12	the X effects. It uses evaluated consistency and the distance from the joint
    13	point measurement to that ordered product. The bound holds first over any
    14	probability law on pairs of line-point pairs and then over a product of restricted
    15	line-point laws, whose point marginal is the uniform pair.
    16	
    17	The estimates hold for arbitrary opposite placements, with first-player
    18	specializations; register commutation requires no symmetry of the state.
    19	The completed-outcome and real-overlap lemmas are also available for other
    20	calculations. The concrete X-deficit argument is separate, in
    21	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.ConcreteXDeficit`.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	The Z deficit supports blueprint `lem:claim-17-3-direct-real`, alongside the
    26	source `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the
    28	consistency input is `lem:qld-xz-lines` and the ordered products are those of
    29	`lem:qld-4-10`.
    30	-/

    43	/-- A sum over completed outcome pairs of a function vanishing on both `none`
    44	classes is the sum over the uncompleted pairs. -/
    45	theorem sum_option_prod_eq_of_none {β γ : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    46	    (F : Option β × Option γ → ℝ) (h1 : ∀ o2, F (none, o2) = 0)
    47	    (h2 : ∀ o1, F (o1, none) = 0) :
    48	    (∑ o, F o) = ∑ bc : β × γ, F (some bc.1, some bc.2) := by
    49	  calc (∑ o : Option β × Option γ, F o)
    50	      = ∑ o1 : Option β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (o1, o2) := Fintype.sum_prod_type (f := F)
    51	    _ = (∑ o2 : Option γ, F (none, o2)) +
    52	          ∑ b : β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (some b, o2) := Fintype.sum_option _
    53	    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (some b, o2) := by
    54	        rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero fun o2 _ => h1 o2, zero_add]
    55	    _ = ∑ b : β, (F (some b, none) + ∑ c : γ, F (some b, some c)) :=
    56	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => Fintype.sum_option _
    57	    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ c : γ, F (some b, some c) := by
    58	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
    59	        rw [h2 (some b), zero_add]
    60	    _ = ∑ bc : β × γ, F (some bc.1, some bc.2) :=
    61	        (Fintype.sum_prod_type (f := fun bc : β × γ => F (some bc.1, some bc.2))).symm
    62	
    63	/-- The completed joint measurement has the joint effect on a pair of
    64	evaluations. -/
    65	theorem completedPair_effect_some {β γ d : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    66	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    67	    (Q : Measurement (β × γ) d) (bc : β × γ) :
    68	    (Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect (some bc.1, some bc.2) =
    69	      Q.effect bc := by
    70	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
    71	    show (Finset.univ.filter fun cd : β × γ =>
    72	        (some cd.1, some cd.2) = (some bc.1, some bc.2)) = {bc} by
    73	      ext cd; simp [Prod.ext_iff, eq_comm]]
    74	  simp

    76	/-- The completed joint measurement vanishes on outcomes outside the image of
    77	the completion. -/
    78	theorem completedPair_effect_eq_zero {β γ d : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    79	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (Q : Measurement (β × γ) d) (o : Option β × Option γ)
    81	    (ho : ∀ bc : β × γ, (some bc.1, some bc.2) ≠ o) :
    82	    (Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o = 0 := by
    83	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
    84	  exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun bc hbc =>
    85	    absurd (Finset.mem_filter.mp hbc).2 (ho bc)

    87	/-- The completion of a projective joint measurement is projective. -/
    88	theorem completedPair_isProjective {β γ d : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    89	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    90	    (Q : Measurement (β × γ) d) (hQ : Measurement.IsProjective Q) :
    91	    Measurement.IsProjective (Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)) := by
    92	  intro o
    93	  by_cases h : ∃ bc : β × γ, (some bc.1, some bc.2) = o
    94	  · obtain ⟨bc, rfl⟩ := h
    95	    rw [completedPair_effect_some]
    96	    exact hQ bc
    97	  · push Not at h
    98	    rw [completedPair_effect_eq_zero Q o h]
    99	    exact IsStarProjection.zero _

   107	    {E : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)} (hE : IsProj E) :
   108	    IsProj (S.place p E) := by

   117	theorem pointMeasExpOption_isProj (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   118	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   119	    (o : Option (PauliScalar P)) :
   120	    IsProj ((S.pointMeasExpOption side W u).effect o) := by

   122	  | none =>
   123	    rw [S.pointMeasExpOption_effect_none]

   130	only on outcome pairs with two evaluations, so their placed state-dependent
   131	squared distance is the one of the joint point measurement and the point
   132	product.  Blueprint `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2651-2698`. -/
   133	theorem sum_norm_place_completedPair_sub_sq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   134	    (p : Placement)
   135	    (Q : Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
   136	    (Gc : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P) →
   137	      Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
   138	    (G : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
   139	    (hsome : ∀ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P, Gc (some ab.1, some ab.2) = G ab)
   140	    (hnone1 : ∀ o2, Gc (none, o2) = 0) (hnone2 : ∀ o1, Gc (o1, none) = 0) :
   141	    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
   142	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   143	          (S.place p ((Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o) -
   144	            S.place p (Gc o)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) =
   145	      ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   146	        ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (Q.effect ab) - S.place p (G ab))
   147	          S.psiHat‖ ^ 2 := by
   148	  refine Eq.trans (sum_option_prod_eq_of_none _ ?_ ?_) ?_
   149	  · intro o2

   151	      place_zero, sub_self]

   155	      place_zero, sub_self]
   156	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   157	  · refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ab _ => ?_
   158	    rw [completedPair_effect_some, hsome]

   162	theorem completedPair_norm_sq_sum_ZX (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) {δ : ℝ}

   191	/-! ## The abstract one-point deficit -/
   192	
   193	/-- Let `A` be a complete measurement, `Q` a projective measurement, `R` a
   194	family of projections and `W` a family of operators, all indexed by the same
   195	outcomes, with `Q`, `R` and `W` commuting with the effects of `A` and with
   196	`W R = W`.  If `A` and `Q` are consistent with defect at most `η` and `Q` is
   197	within squared distance `ζ` of `Wᴴ`, then the deficit of the overlap of `A`
   198	with `R` is at most `2 √η + 2 √ζ`.  The proof inserts `Q` before `R`, replaces
   199	`Q R` by `W R = W`, and compares `W` with `Q`; each of the three steps is a
   200	Cauchy--Schwarz estimate weighted by `A`.  This is the common estimate behind
   201	the deficits in the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
   202	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1239`. -/
   203	theorem one_sub_overlap_le_of_consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
   204	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   205	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   206	    (μ : Distribution X) (A Q : X → Measurement α ι) (R W : X → α → Op ι)
   207	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
   208	    (hQ : ∀ x, Measurement.IsProjective (Q x)) (hR : ∀ x a, IsProj (R x a))
   209	    (hAQ : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((Q x).effect a))
   210	    (hAR : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (R x a))
   211	    (hAW : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (W x a))
   212	    (hWR : ∀ x a, W x a * R x a = W x a)
   213	    (hnonneg : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a))
   214	    (η ζ : ℝ)
   215	    (hcons : consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => (A x).effect a)
   216	      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) ψ ≤ η)
   217	    (hdist : opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => (Q x).effect a)
   218	      (fun x a => (W x a)ᴴ) ψ ≤ ζ) :
   219	    1 - avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a)) ≤
   220	      2 * Real.sqrt η + 2 * Real.sqrt ζ := by
   221	  set ovQ := avgOver μ (fun x =>
   222	    ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a)) with hovQ
   223	  have h1 : 1 - ovQ ≤ η := by
   224	    rw [← consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap μ A Q ψ hμ hψ]
   225	    exact hcons
   226	  have hovQ_nonneg : 0 ≤ ovQ :=
   227	    avgOver_nonneg μ _ fun x => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => hnonneg x a
   228	  have hovQ_le : ovQ ≤ 1 :=
   229	    avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one μ A (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) ψ hμ hψ
   230	      (fun x a => hQ x a) hAQ
   231	  have h1' : 1 - ovQ ≤ Real.sqrt η := by
   232	    have h0 : 0 ≤ 1 - ovQ := by linarith
   233	    calc 1 - ovQ = Real.sqrt ((1 - ovQ) ^ 2) := (Real.sqrt_sq h0).symm
   234	      _ ≤ Real.sqrt η := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (by nlinarith)
   235	  -- comparing `Q` with `W` under the weight `A`
   236	  have hWconj : ∀ x a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a) =
   237	      stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (W x a)ᴴ) := by
   238	    intro x a
   239	    rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a),
   240	      Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, measurement_effect_hermitian]
   241	    congr 1
   242	    have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose (hAW x a).eq
   243	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
   244	      measurement_effect_hermitian] at h
   245	    exact h
   246	  have h2 : |ovQ - avgOver μ (fun x =>
   247	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a))| ≤ Real.sqrt ζ := by
   248	    rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hWconj x a]
   249	    exact abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_of_opFamilyDistSq μ A
   250	      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) (fun x a => (W x a)ᴴ) ψ hμ hψ ζ hdist
   251	  -- replacing `Q R` by `W R = W`
   252	  have h4 : |avgOver μ (fun x =>
   253	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
   254	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a))| ≤
   255	      Real.sqrt ζ := by
   256	    have hpt : ∀ x,
   257	        (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
   258	          (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a)) =
   259	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (((Q x).effect a - W x a) * R x a)) := by
   260	      intro x
   261	      rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   262	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   263	      rw [sub_mul, hWR]
   264	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
   265	    rw [← avgOver_sub, avgOver_congr μ _ _ hpt]
   266	    have hcs := abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_sqrt_of_isProj' μ A
   267	      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a - W x a) R ψ hμ hψ hR hAR
   268	      (fun x a => (hAQ x a).sub_right (hAW x a))
   269	    refine hcs.trans (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt ?_)
   270	    have hdist' : avgOver μ (fun x =>
   271	        ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState ((Q x).effect a - (W x a)ᴴ) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤ ζ :=
   272	      hdist
   273	    refine le_of_eq_of_le ?_ hdist'
   274	    refine avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   275	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, measurement_effect_hermitian]
   276	  -- inserting `Q` before `R`
   277	  have h5 : |avgOver μ (fun x =>
   278	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
   279	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a))| ≤
   280	      Real.sqrt η := by
   281	    have hpt : ∀ x,
   282	        (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a)) -
   283	          (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) =
   284	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((1 - (Q x).effect a) * R x a)) := by
   285	      intro x

usage: blueprint_leanok_axioms.py [-h] [--repo-root REPO_ROOT] [--lake LAKE]
                                  [--skip-axiom-check] [--ci]
                                  [--warn-missing-leanok]

Blueprint ``\leanok`` axiom-closure checker. This script audits the blueprint
chapters against the Lean codebase. For each unique declaration referenced by
``\lean{...}`` in ``blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex`` it: * checks that the
declaration exists in the Lean source tree; * if any blueprint entry for that
declaration carries ``\leanok`` on the statement or proof, runs ``#print
axioms`` and fails on any transitive dependency on ``sorryAx``; * optionally
warns when a blueprint declaration is sorry-free in Lean but lacks any
``\leanok`` tag (enable ``--warn-missing-leanok``). The checker imports only
the Lean modules that define the referenced blueprint declarations, rather
than importing the top-level ``MIPStarRE`` barrel. This keeps the rebuild
scope small and avoids stale-barrel issues. Use ``--skip-axiom-check`` for a
fast parse-only smoke test. Use ``--ci`` to exit with status 1 when any
``\leanok`` declaration fails the axiom audit.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --repo-root REPO_ROOT
                        Repository root (default: parent of this script)
  --lake LAKE           Path to the lake executable (default: lake)
  --skip-axiom-check    Parse blueprint references only; skip the Lean axiom
                        audit.
  --ci                  Exit with status 1 when any \leanok declaration fails
                        the audit.
  --warn-missing-leanok
                        Also audit non-\leanok declarations and warn when they
                        are sorry-free.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
r"""Check blueprint LaTeX source conventions.

The blueprint intentionally avoids ``cleveref``.  The original paper uses
``\Cref`` and related commands extensively, but the blueprint should spell out
the reference type explicitly and then use ordinary ``\ref`` or ``\eqref``.
This keeps the print and web builds independent of ``cleveref``.

Remark environments are also expository, not proof-bearing blueprint nodes.
They should not carry ``\lean{}``, ``\leanok``, or ``\uses{}`` metadata; such
metadata belongs on definitions, lemmas, propositions, theorems, and corollaries.
Labels declared inside remarks should likewise not occur as targets of
``\uses{}``, since a remark is not a theorem-like dependency.  This rule is
semantic in the modest sense needed here: it follows the labels actually
declared in remark environments, rather than relying on a naming convention such
as a ``rem:`` prefix.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from tex_utils import strip_tex_comment


BLUEPRINT_EXTENSIONS = {".tex", ".sty", ".cls"}
FORBIDDEN_CLEVEREF = re.compile(r"cleveref|\\[cC]ref")
FORBIDDEN_REMARK_METADATA = re.compile(r"\\lean\{|\\leanok\b|\\uses\{")
BEGIN_REMARK = re.compile(r"\\begin\s*\{\s*remark\*?\s*\}")
END_REMARK = re.compile(r"\\end\s*\{\s*remark\*?\s*\}")
LABEL = re.compile(r"\\label\s*\{\s*([^}\s]+)\s*\}")
USES_BEGIN = re.compile(r"\\uses\s*\{")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Finding:
    """A forbidden active source fragment in a blueprint file."""

    path: Path
    line: int
    column: int
    fragment: str


def iter_source_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """Return blueprint source files checked for LaTeX conventions."""

    return sorted(
        path
        for path in root.rglob("*")
        if path.is_file() and path.suffix in BLUEPRINT_EXTENSIONS
    )


def find_cleveref_usage(root: Path) -> list[Finding]:
    """Find active uses of cleveref package names or reference commands."""

    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for path in iter_source_files(root):
        for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
            active_line = strip_tex_comment(raw_line)
            for match in FORBIDDEN_CLEVEREF.finditer(active_line):
                findings.append(
                    Finding(
                        path=path,
                        line=line_number,
                        column=match.start() + 1,
                        fragment=match.group(0),
                    )
                )
    return findings


def find_remark_metadata(root: Path) -> list[Finding]:
    """Find Lean or dependency metadata inside remark environments."""

    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for path in iter_source_files(root):
        remark_depth = 0
        for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
            active_line = strip_tex_comment(raw_line)
            in_remark_at_line_start = remark_depth > 0
            remark_depth += len(BEGIN_REMARK.findall(active_line))

            if in_remark_at_line_start or remark_depth > 0:
                for match in FORBIDDEN_REMARK_METADATA.finditer(active_line):
                    findings.append(
                        Finding(
                            path=path,
                            line=line_number,
                            column=match.start() + 1,
                            fragment=match.group(0),
                        )
                    )

            remark_depth = max(0, remark_depth - len(END_REMARK.findall(active_line)))
    return findings


def collect_remark_labels(root: Path) -> dict[str, Finding]:
    """Return labels declared inside remark environments."""

    labels: dict[str, Finding] = {}
    for path in iter_source_files(root):
        remark_depth = 0
        for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
            active_line = strip_tex_comment(raw_line)
            in_remark_at_line_start = remark_depth > 0
            remark_depth += len(BEGIN_REMARK.findall(active_line))

            if in_remark_at_line_start or remark_depth > 0:
                for match in LABEL.finditer(active_line):
                    label = match.group(1)
                    labels.setdefault(
                        label,
                        Finding(
                            path=path,
                            line=line_number,
                            column=match.start(1) + 1,
                            fragment=label,
                        ),
                    )

            remark_depth = max(0, remark_depth - len(END_REMARK.findall(active_line)))
    return labels


def iter_uses_targets(path: Path) -> list[Finding]:
    r"""Return dependency targets appearing in active ``\uses{...}`` commands."""

    findings: list[Finding] = []
    collecting = False
    start_line = 0
    start_column = 0
    buffer: list[str] = []

    for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
        active_line = strip_tex_comment(raw_line)
        index = 0
        while index <= len(active_line):
            if not collecting:
                match = USES_BEGIN.search(active_line, index)
                if match is None:
                    break
                collecting = True
                start_line = line_number
                start_column = match.start() + 1
                buffer = []
                index = match.end()

            end_index = active_line.find("}", index)
            if end_index == -1:
                buffer.append(active_line[index:])
                buffer.append("\n")
                break

            buffer.append(active_line[index:end_index])
            uses_body = "".join(buffer)
            for target in uses_body.split(","):
                target = target.strip()
                if target:
                    findings.append(
                        Finding(
                            path=path,
                            line=start_line,
                            column=start_column,
                            fragment=target,
                        )
                    )
            collecting = False
            buffer = []
            index = end_index + 1

    return findings

   874	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for coefficient polynomial agreement]
   875		\label{lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement}

   883		$f,g\in K^{c+1}$ be distinct coefficient vectors. Their polynomials
   884		$p_f(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}f_iT^i$ and $p_g(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}g_iT^i$
   885		agree at at most $c$ elements of $K$.

   887		and has natural degree at most $c$.

   889		in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}
   890		(\texttt{14\_analysis\_of\_the\_pauli\_basis\_test.tex:955}).

   894		\leanok
   895		The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
   896		and gives polynomials of degree at most $c$. If the polynomials agreed
   897		at more than $c$ elements, the univariate root bound applied to their
   898		difference would force them to be equal, contradicting $f\ne g$.

  1429	\begin{lemma}[The sub-line distribution]
  1430		\label{lem:qld-sublines}

  1435		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, lem:qld-sublines). The
  1436		% line-point distribution over F_q^{2m+2} is built from the index
  1437		% function chi of def:ld-question-distribution at dimension 2m+2, which
  1438		% is defined only when 2m+2 divides q; the source instantiates it
  1439		% without securing this condition. See rem:qld-4-7-divisibility.
  1440		There exists a distribution $D$
  1441		over tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, where $\ell$ is a line in
  1442		$\F_q^{2m+2}$ and $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ are lines in $\F_q^m$, with the
  1443		following properties:
  1444		\begin{enumerate}
  1445			\item The marginal distribution over $\ell$ is the same as the
  1446			marginal of the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
  1447			% The source phrases the next property as: the marginal over
  1448			% (ell_X, ell_Z) is "a mixture of the product distributions
  1449			% D_{ALine,i} x D_{ALine,j} and D_{DLine,i} x D_{DLine,j}". Those
  1450			% products are distributions over pairs of line-point pairs, not
  1451			% over pairs of lines, so the phrase does not define the asserted
  1452			% marginal distribution on pairs of lines as written; the
  1453			% formulation below states the mixture at the level of the joint
  1454			% law of (ell_X, ell_Z, u), which is what the proofs of
  1455			% lem:claim-17-2 and lem:claim-17-3 use.
  1456			\item For any point of the form $u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$
  1457			lying on $\ell$, it holds that $u_X \in \ell_X$ and
  1458			$u_Z \in \ell_Z$. Moreover, the joint distribution of
  1459			$(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$, for $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z) \sim D$ and
  1460			$u$ chosen uniformly at random on $\ell$, is a mixture of
  1461			components indexed by a type
  1462			$\mathrm{v} \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and indices
  1463			$i, j \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ with the following two properties
  1464			within the component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$: the pair
  1465			$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is distributed according to the product of the
  1466			marginal distributions on lines of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and of
  1467			$D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the
  1468			point $u_X$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_X$ and likewise the
  1469			point $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_Z$. Equivalently,
  1470			since under each restricted distribution the point is uniformly
  1471			distributed on the line conditionally on the line: within the
  1472			component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$, the pair
  1473			$((\ell_X, u_X), (\ell_Z, z'))$, where $z'$ is a uniformly random
  1474			point of $\ell_Z$ sampled independently of $u$, is distributed
  1475			according to $D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and
  1476			symmetrically the pair $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, u_Z))$, with $x'$
  1477			a uniformly random point of $\ell_X$ sampled independently of
  1478			$u$, is distributed according to
  1479			$D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$. (No assertion is made
  1480			about the joint conditional law of the pair $(u_X, u_Z)$.)

  1482			axis-parallel.

  1492		$(\ell, u)$ from the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and write
  1493		$u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$, so that Property~1 holds by
  1494		construction; all auxiliary randomness introduced below is sampled
  1495		independently of $(\ell, u)$. As in
  1496		Definition~\ref{def:ith-restricted-line}, write $\bar\chi$ for the
  1497		zero-based shift of the index function at dimension $m$. Its classes
  1498		$\bar\chi^{-1}(i)$ for $i \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ partition $\F_q$
  1499		into sets of equal size $q/m$. Write $\bar\chi_{2m+2}$ for the analogous
  1500		zero-based shift at dimension $2m+2$. For the extended-coordinate index in
  1501		the construction below, write $k=r-1$ when the paper writes $r$; the
  1502		source-line indices $i_X,i_Z$ are shifted in the same way. The function
  1503		$\bar\chi_{2m+2}$ is defined only when $2m+2$ divides $q$, and hence so is
  1504		the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ from which $(\ell, u)$ is
  1505		drawn
  1506		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}); admissibility of
  1507		$(q,m,d)$ supplies only that $m$ divides $q$, and for admissible
  1508		parameters with $m \ge 2$ the required divisibility fails, so this
  1509		first step is an unresolved obligation of the source argument, recorded
  1510		in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and analyzed in
  1511		\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; the construction below is
  1512		carried out for the parameters for which the distribution is defined.
  1513		By a
  1514		\emph{fresh diagonal direction pair} we mean a pair $(s', w')$ with
  1515		$s'$ uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $w' \in \F_q^m$ having coordinates
  1516		$0, \dots, \bar\chi(s')-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates
  1517		uniformly random; this is exactly the law of the coordinate--direction
  1518		data of the diagonal component of the line-point distribution over
  1519		$\F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}).
  1520	
  1521		If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, $\ell = (v, e_k)$ with
  1522		$v = (v_X, v_Z, \alpha_0, \beta_0)$ and $k \in \{0, \dots, 2m+1\}$, set
  1523		$\ell_X = (v'_X, e_{i_X})$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, e_{i_Z})$ where: for
  1524		$0 \le k < m$, $i_X = k$ and $i_Z$ is uniformly random in
  1525		$\{0,\dots,m-1\}$; for $m \le k < 2m$, $i_X$ is uniformly random and
  1526		$i_Z = k - m$; for $2m \le k < 2m+2$, both $i_X$ and $i_Z$ are
  1527		uniformly random; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are the canonical line
  1528		representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the chosen directions
  1529		(Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}), so that $v_X \in \ell_X$
  1530		and $v_Z \in \ell_Z$.
  1531	
  1532		If $\ell$ is diagonal, $\ell = (v, s, w)$, then by the construction of
  1533		the diagonal component of the line-point distribution
  1534		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} instantiated at
  1535		dimension $2m+2$) the direction $w = (w_X, w_Z, \gamma, \delta)$ has
  1536		coordinates $0, \dots, k-1$ equal to $0$, where
  1537		$k = \bar\chi_{2m+2}(s)$,
  1538		and its remaining coordinates are uniformly random. These remaining
  1539		coordinates may also vanish, so $w$ need not have a nonzero coordinate
  1540		at index $k$ and may be the zero vector, in which case $\ell$ is a
  1541		singleton (Definition~\ref{def:line}).
  1542		% In its one-based notation, the source proof describes w as "a direction
  1543		% vector whose first nonzero coordinate is j = chi(s)"
  1544		% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, proof
  1545		% of lem:qld-sublines); the distribution delivers only the weaker
  1546		% property recorded here, which is the one the argument uses. The
  1547		% source also leaves the laws of s_X and s_Z unspecified ("chosen such
  1548		% that chi(s_X) = j" in its one-based notation); the uniform choices
  1549		% below are needed for the exact marginals claimed in Property 2.
  1550		Sample $\ell_X = (v'_X, s_X, w'_X)$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, s_Z, w'_Z)$
  1551		where: for $0 \le k < m$, $w'_X = w_X$ and $w'_Z = w_Z$, with $s_X$
  1552		uniformly random in the class $\bar\chi^{-1}(k)$ and $s_Z$ uniformly
  1553		random in the class $\bar\chi^{-1}(0)$; for $m \le k < 2m$, the pair
  1554		$(s_X, w'_X)$ is a fresh diagonal direction pair and $w'_Z = w_Z$,
  1555		with $s_Z$ uniformly random in the class $\bar\chi^{-1}(k-m)$; for
  1556		$2m \le k < 2m+2$, both $(s_X, w'_X)$ and $(s_Z, w'_Z)$ are fresh
  1557		diagonal direction pairs, sampled independently; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are
  1558		the canonical representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the directions
  1559		$w'_X, w'_Z$.

  1561		Property~3 is immediate from the procedure: when $\ell$ is
  1562		axis-parallel, both $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are constructed to be
  1563		axis-parallel. The containments in Property~2 hold for every point
  1564		$u^\dagger = (u^\dagger_X, u^\dagger_Z, \alpha^\dagger,
  1565		\beta^\dagger)$ of $\ell$: the block $u^\dagger_X$ differs from $v_X$
  1566		by a multiple of the direction of $\ell_X$ when that direction is
  1567		inherited from $\ell$ (namely $e_k$ for axis-parallel $\ell$ with
  1568		$0 \le k < m$, and $w_X$ for diagonal $\ell$ with $0 \le k < m$),
  1569		and equals $v_X$ in all other cases, since then the corresponding
  1570		block of the direction of $\ell$ vanishes; in either case
  1571		$u^\dagger_X \in \ell_X$ because $v_X \in \ell_X$, and symmetrically
  1572		$u^\dagger_Z \in \ell_Z$.

  1575		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is a function of $\ell$ and of the auxiliary
  1576		randomness alone: the directions used are either read off from the
  1577		direction data of $\ell$ or freshly sampled, and by
  1578		Proposition~\ref{prop:line-equiv} the canonical representatives
  1579		$v'_X, v'_Z$ do not depend on which base point of $\ell$ is used to
  1580		compute them. Under both components of the line-point distribution the
  1581		point $u$ is uniformly distributed on $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and, conditioned
  1582		on the line $\ell$, uniformly distributed on the points of $\ell$
  1583		(each of the $q$ values of the line parameter, or the single point
  1584		when the direction vanishes, being equally likely). Hence, conditioned
  1585		on $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the sampled point $u$ is uniformly
  1586		distributed on $\ell$, and it suffices to establish the claimed
  1587		mixture description for the tuple $(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$ produced by
  1588		the procedure itself.
  1589	
  1590		Condition on the component of the line-point distribution
  1591		(axis-parallel or diagonal) and on $k$; the mixture of Property~2 is
  1592		over these choices together with the fresh index choices, and the
  1593		blocks $u_X, u_Z$ of $u$ are independent and uniform on $\F_q^m$,
  1594		independent of all direction data. In the axis-parallel case with
  1595		$0 \le k < m$, the pair $(\ell_X, u_X)$ consists of the uniformly
  1596		random point $u_X$ together with the canonical axis-parallel line
  1597		through it in direction $e_k$, so
  1598		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},k}$, while, conditioned
  1599		additionally on $i_Z$, the pair $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ consists of the
  1600		uniformly random point $u_Z$ together with the canonical line through
  1601		it in direction $e_{i_Z}$, so
  1602		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},i_Z}$; the two pairs are
  1603		functions of the disjoint independent data $u_X$ and $(u_Z, i_Z)$,
  1604		hence independent. In the diagonal case with $0 \le k < m$, the
  1605		triple $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ has $u_X$ uniform, $w_X$ with coordinates
  1606		$0, \dots, k-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates uniform,
  1607		and $s_X$ uniform in $\bar\chi^{-1}(k)$, which is exactly the law
  1608		generating $D_{\mathrm{DLine},k}$; hence
  1609		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},k}$, and similarly
  1610		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},0}$ since $w_Z$ is uniform and
  1611		$s_Z$ is uniform in $\bar\chi^{-1}(0)$; the two pairs are functions of
  1612		the disjoint independent data $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ and $(u_Z, w_Z, s_Z)$,
  1613		hence independent. The remaining cases are analogous: each of
  1614		$(\ell_X, u_X)$ and $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ is either built from the inherited
  1615		direction block as above, or from a fresh axis index or fresh diagonal
  1616		direction pair, in which case it is distributed as the uniform mixture
  1617		over $i \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ for the
  1618		corresponding type $\mathrm{v}$; and the two pairs are always functions of
  1619		disjoint independent collections of the variables $u_X$, $u_Z$, the
  1620		direction blocks, and the fresh auxiliary choices, hence independent
  1621		conditioned on the component. Within each component this yields exactly the
  1622		description of Property~2: the pair $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is
  1623		product-distributed according to the line marginals of
  1624		$D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and $D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on
  1625		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, each of $u_X$ and $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed
  1626		on its line, because under each restricted distribution the point is
  1627		uniform on the line conditionally on the line. The equivalent product
  1628		formulations follow from the same conditional uniformity.

  1681	\begin{definition}[Directly indexed sub-line laws]
  1682		\label{def:direct-subline-law}
  1683		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SubLineWitness}
  1684		\leanok
  1685		\uses{def:ith-restricted-line-refined, def:line-representative,
  1686			def:combine-map}
  1687		Put $n=2m+2$. The directly indexed extended line-point law samples
  1688		$i\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ and $u,v\in\F_q^n$ independently and uniformly,
  1689		and chooses the axis or diagonal kind with equal probabilities.
  1690		For the axis kind set $w=e_i$; for the diagonal kind set $w_j=0$ for
  1691		$j<i$ and $w_j=v_j$ for $j\ge i$. The line has base $L_w^{\mathrm{lnf}}(u)$
  1692		and direction $w$, retaining its kind and coordinate index; the sampled
  1693		point is $u$. Zero diagonal directions are included.
  1694	
  1695		A directly indexed sub-line law $D_{\mathrm{dir}}$ is a probability law
  1696		on triples $(\ell,\ell_X,\ell_Z)$ with the following properties.
  1697		Its extended-line marginal is the line marginal just defined.
  1698		Every supported triple admits affine maps $t\mapsto a_W+b_Wt$ such that
  1699		\[
  1700			\pi_W(\ell(t))=\ell_W(a_W+b_Wt),\qquad W\in\{X,Z\},
  1701		\]
  1702		where $\ell(t)$ denotes base plus parameter times direction and the
  1703		field identifications are understood. Thus each extended point projects
  1704		onto its two source lines, with affine scalar coordinates $\alpha(t)$
  1705		and $\beta(t)$ as in Definition~\ref{def:combine-map}. An axis-parallel
  1706		extended line has axis-parallel source lines.
  1707	
  1708		Finally there is one probability law on
  1709		$(\mathrm v,i,j)\in\{\mathrm{ALine},\mathrm{DLine}\}
  1710		\times\{0,\dots,m-1\}^2$ with the following two mixture properties.
  1711		Sample a triple from $D_{\mathrm{dir}}$ and an independent uniform
  1712		parameter $t$ on $\ell$. The law of $(\ell_X,\ell_Z,\pi_X(\ell(t)))$
  1713		is the mixture obtained by sampling $(\ell_X,x)$ from the seed-bearing
  1714		restriction $\widetilde D_{\mathrm v,i}$ of
  1715		Definition~\ref{def:ith-restricted-line-refined} and independently
  1716		$\ell_Z$ from the line marginal of $\widetilde D_{\mathrm v,j}$, and
  1717		retaining $(\ell_X,\ell_Z,x)$.
  1718		The law of $(\ell_X,\ell_Z,\pi_Z(\ell(t)))$ is the mixture obtained
  1719		by retaining $(\ell_X,\ell_Z,z)$ from the corresponding independent
  1720		samples of $\ell_X$ and $(\ell_Z,z)$. These are separate one-point
  1721		marginal identities over the seed-bearing restrictions, with the same
  1722		mixture weights for both projected marginals; they impose no
  1723		joint conditional independence of the two projected points.
  1724		Identification with the source restrictions $D_{\mathrm v,i}$, and with
  1725		the source law $D$, is a separate obligation;
  1726		see \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}.
  1727	\end{definition}

+\section{Scalar estimates on the auxiliary subline law}
+\label{sec:auxiliary-subline-scalars}
+
+Claims \path{claim:17-1} and \path{claim:17-3} use the distribution $D$
+of the source subline lemma. Their formal counterparts currently use a
+different distribution $D_{\rm dir}$, represented by
+\leanid{SubLineWitness}: the extended line is directly indexed, its marginal
+is that of \leanid{directLinePointDist}, and its separate X and Z point
+marginals are mixtures of refined seed-bearing restricted line-point laws,
+represented by \leanid{restrictedALineDist} and \leanid{restrictedDLineDist}.
+These are the laws of blueprint \path{def:ith-restricted-line-refined}, not
+the source restrictions of \path{def:ith-restricted-line}. Identifying their
+source push-forwards, including forgetting the residual seed on axis lines,
+remains open. Existence of this auxiliary distribution does not identify it
+with $D$. In particular,
+sampling a coordinate index directly does not construct the seed-indexed
+extended-line questions where the divisibility condition above fails.%
+\footnote{The claims are at lines 1140--1166 and 1204--1239 of
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}.
+The restricted formal results are
+\leanid{subline\_replace\_by\_ordered\_product} and
+\leanid{subline\_Z\_term\_near\_one} in
+\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Claims.lean}; their scope is tracked by
+\ghissue{387} and PR \#400.}
+
+There is also a distinction in the scalar conclusion. Let $A_Q(D)$,
+$A_{ZX}(D)$ and $A_Z(D)$ denote the averaged joint-point, ordered-product,
+and Z-point overlaps in these claims. The source assertions are
+\[
+ |A_Q(D)-A_{ZX}(D)|=O(\sqrt{\delta_Q}),\qquad
+ |A_Z(D)-1|=O\bigl(\sqrt m\,
+   (\delta_P^{1/4}+\delta_Q^{1/4}+\eps^{1/4})\bigr).
+\]
+For projective joint point measurements and complete paired-line
+measurements satisfying the witness hypotheses, and
+any auxiliary subline witness, the established statements instead bound
+\[
+ |\operatorname{Re}A_Q(D_{\rm dir})-
+     \operatorname{Re}A_{ZX}(D_{\rm dir})|\le2\sqrt{\delta_Q},\qquad
+ |\operatorname{Re}A_Z(D_{\rm dir})-1|\le
+ 2\sqrt m\,(\delta_P^{1/4}+\delta_Q^{1/4}+\eps^{1/4}).
+\]
+Their evaluations use the completed answer alphabet: an undefined
+evaluation contributes zero point effect. The joint-point and paired-line
+witnesses retain their stated consistency and degree hypotheses; neither
+new transport data nor a reality assumption is imposed on these results.
+
+The ordered product $M_ZM_X$ need not be Hermitian. Thus a real-part bound
+alone does not establish the first source assertion. With
+$W=Q-M_ZM_X$, the Cauchy--Schwarz argument bounds the second squared factor
+using $W^\dagger W$, not $W^2$. The same-placement squared distance is at
+most $4\delta_Q$, obtained by inserting the opposite-placement joint
+measurement and applying the squared-distance triangle inequality. This
+gives $2\sqrt{\delta_Q}$, which preserves the source's asymptotic order.
+The complex Cauchy--Schwarz estimate still needs a formal proof; an
+assumption that the ordered overlap is real would not replace it.
+
+The remaining obligations have distinct mathematical content. The proposed
+target \leanid{subline\_source\_distribution\_transport} must construct
+the seed-indexed law where it is defined and prove the corresponding
+pushforward, evaluation, and separate point-marginal identities; the
+unrestricted source domain still requires resolution of the definition-level
+obstruction above. The proposed target
+\leanid{subline\_complex\_overlap\_bound} must prove the complex modulus
+estimate from positivity, completeness, the point marginal, and the
+same-placement distance, without an added reality hypothesis. For the Z
+overlap, positivity of the two commuting opposite-placement factors gives
+reality, which must also be recorded when passing from the real-part result
+to the source scalar statement. These are named future proof targets, not
+assumed or axiomatized declarations.
+
+The blueprint therefore leaves both source-labelled claims pending and
+records the proved auxiliary results separately, with their carrier,
+completed evaluations, measurement hypotheses, and real-part conclusions
+explicit. Their Lean statements and proofs are retained. No new proof hole
+is introduced by this scope correction, and the existing Claim 17-2 proof
+obligation is unchanged. Discharge requires the transport and complex
+estimate just described; the auxiliary results do not certify them.
+
